name: Matrichakra
description: A star 52 parsecs away, 7.2 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 77512: radius 7.167 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 36.192 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.049) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 77512: effective temperature 5292 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.043)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 77512: distance 52.138 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.014), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 52 parsecs away, 7.2 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 36 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,292 K, so 7.167 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 77512: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Delta Coronae Borealis
quotes.card: Delta Coronae Borealis is a variable star in the constellation of Corona Borealis.
quotes.introduction: It has the proper name Matrichakra; Delta Coronae Borealis is its Bayer designation, which is Latinized from δ Coronae Borealis and abbreviated Delta CrB or δ CrB.
